text.name: Aethermancer
text.lore: He learned young to let aether take the blows meant for his flesh. Now he draws on it for every battle, pushing his exhausted body beyond its limits. He knows what the power is costing him. He still believes he has the better bargain.
text.blurb: Uses mana to absorb damage. His talents can strengthen this protection, spend mana for added Cold damage or recover mana by dealing damage.
text.short: Regenerates an additional 2.5% of maximum Mana per second. 10% of damage taken is absorbed by Mana before Life.

text.name: Alchemist
text.lore: He came down here for the water. Something in the rock changes what is steeped in it, and he has tested it on everything, including his own blood. Years of experiments have left him sallow and half-poisoned. He still trusts his brews to carry him through the next fight.
text.blurb: A flask specialist whose talents grant combat bonuses during flask effects, improve recovery and replenish Charges.
text.short: Every 8 kills restore 1 Charge to each flask.

text.name: Rogue
text.lore: Obreth keeps his ties to the Obsidian Order quiet. They sent him into the depths to read the rock; he returned with two knives and has been trading up ever since. He has little patience for those who hide behind shields. Whatever the Order sent him to find, he keeps to himself.
text.blurb: The only character who can dual wield. His talents reward weapon pairings, strengthen opening hits and grant bonuses after kills.
text.short: Can equip a one-handed weapon in each hand.
says: Both hands may hold a one-handed weapon. A pair puts 75% of the main hand and 55% of the off hand into every hit, and the rate ALTERNATES: this swing at the main hand’s, the next at the off hand’s.

text.name: Warrior
text.lore: Mahthar seeks neither riches nor answers in the depths. The marks on his skin are older than these workings, and he cuts a new one after every worthy fight. He wears them openly in the warmth of the rock, trusting them more than any armour.
text.blurb: A weapon specialist with talents for shield defence, retaliation on Block and powerful two-handed attacks.
text.short: Hits can Stun enemies for 1.1s. The chance increases with the proportion of the target's maximum Life dealt as damage.

text.name: Ailment
text.means: A temporary effect that deals damage over time or weakens a target. Your hits can apply the Ailment associated with their damage type; Poison requires a source that specifically applies it. Each 100% application chance guarantees one stack, with the remainder rolled for another. A target can carry 12 Ailment stacks in total; a new stack replaces the oldest at the cap. Resistance reduces Ailment damage of the corresponding type. Armour does not normally reduce Ailment damage.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/data.ts`: `AILMENT`, `AILMENTS`; `src/sim/run.ts`: `applyTyped`, `strike`, `applyAilment`, `stepAilments`, `hide`; hero typed-hit chance, guaranteed stacks plus remainder, shared 12-stack cap with oldest replacement, resistance and Second Skin exception.

text.name: Arc
text.means: Allows a Projectile to jump from the last enemy hit to the nearest enemy it has not hit, within 4.5 tiles. Each Arc adds one jump. By default, every Arc deals 70% of the full hit damage; this share does not decrease on each jump. Skills and modifiers can change the share or make successive Arcs stronger.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/skills.ts`: `projectile`; `src/sim/run.ts`: `stepOrbs`; nearest unhit target from last hit, 4.5 tiles, default 70% of full hit rather than repeated 30% loss; explicit growth overrides.

text.name: Area of Effect
text.means: Scales the area covered by skill effects such as Splash, Clouds and skill-created Bursts. It also extends Cone reach. The bonus applies to area: 100% increased Area of Effect doubles the area and increases radius by about 41%. Area of Effect does not increase damage.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/run.ts`: `areaRadius`; `src/sim/skills.ts`: Splash, Cloud, death Burst and Cone consumers; radius uses square root of area multiplier, 100% area gives about 41% radius, no damage multiplier. Fixed-radius passives are not included in the blanket promise.

text.name: Armour
text.means: Armour reduces damage from hits of every damage type. Additional Armour gives diminishing returns, up to 75% damage reduction. Armour does not normally reduce Ailment damage and does not reduce boss drains.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. W019: `src/data.ts` says 300 Armour reaches half the 75% cap, but `src/sim/stats.ts:armourReduction` returns 50%. Rewrite confirms hit/type scope, diminishing returns and cap, omitting the disputed example. | Returned to pending: decision recorded in BLOCKERS.md.

text.name: Bleed
text.means: Physical hits use your chance to apply Bleed. Each stack you apply deals 22 base Physical damage per second for 5s, before Ailment damage and duration modifiers. Spell Damage, Attack Damage and Critical Damage do not increase this damage.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/data.ts`: Bleed definition; `src/sim/stats.ts`: `ailmentDamage`; `src/sim/run.ts`: `strike`, `stepAilments`, `useSkill.wound`; 22 base Physical DPS for 5s, source modifiers including Exsanguinate apply; no Critical tick damage.

text.name: Block
text.means: Blocking prevents all damage from an ordinary enemy hit. Block Chance is capped at 60%. Ailment damage, boss room attacks and boss drains bypass Block.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/stats.ts`: `blockChance`; `src/sim/run.ts`: `dealDamage`, `bite`, `stepAilments`; 60% cap, ordinary hit negation; boss room damage and Ailment ticks do not roll Block.

text.name: Burn
text.means: Fire hits use your chance to apply Burn. Each stack you apply deals 26 base Fire damage per second for 4s, before Ailment damage and duration modifiers. Spell Damage, Attack Damage and Critical Damage do not increase this damage.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/data.ts`: Burn definition; `src/sim/stats.ts`: `ailmentDamage`, `ailmentChances`; `src/sim/run.ts`: `strike`, `stepAilments`; 26 base Fire DPS per stack for 4s before Ailment modifiers, independent of Attack/Spell/Critical Damage.

text.name: Burst
text.means: An instant circular effect. Damage Bursts hit nearby enemies; Contagion Bursts apply Poison. The source determines the trigger, damage and radius. Effects that make killed enemies Burst can chain through further kills for up to 8 generations. Overlapping Bursts can affect the same enemy.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/skills.ts`: `burstFrom`, `blastAround`; `src/sim/run.ts`: `sunder`, `spreadAilment`, `burstCurse`; sources differ in damage, radius and trigger. Death-hit chains stop after 8 generations. Removed false blanket claims about passive scaling and diameter.

text.name: Charge
text.means: Each flask holds 2 Charges, and each use spends one. Flasks start every descent with full Charges. Charge recovery effects can refill them during a descent, up to their capacity. Unspent Charges do not carry over as extras on the next descent.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/data.ts`: `POTIONS`; `src/sim/run.ts`: constructor, `drink`, `bankCharges`, `stepRecharge`; two per flask per descent, one per use, restoration capped individually, no extra stockpile across descents.

text.name: Chill
text.means: Cold hits use your chance to apply Chill. Chill stacks normally last 3s. Each application Slows Attack and Cast Speed for 3s, based on the current stack count: 6% per stack, up to 75%. Enemies normally Freeze at 8 stacks for 1.4s: they cannot move, attack or cast, and their Chill stacks are removed. The next hit against that enemy is a guaranteed Critical, even while it is Frozen. You Freeze at 3 stacks instead; protection against Chill raises this threshold.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. W018: `src/data.ts` promises movement Slow; `RunSim.chill`, `hasteOf`, `paceOf`, `stepEffects`, `stepAilments`, `freeze` disagree on movement and Slow duration. Confirmed base stacks, Attack/Cast Slow, distinct hero threshold and immediately available guaranteed Critical are clarified; no movement claim added. | Returned to pending: decision recorded in BLOCKERS.md.

text.name: Cloud
text.means: A circular area that applies an Ailment to enemies inside it, with no target limit. An ordinary Blight Cloud applies Poison once when cast; the Poison then lasts for its own duration. Wandering Rot creates a moving Cloud that applies Poison repeatedly. Spore Burst replaces the Poison with a hit. Overlapping Clouds can affect the same enemy.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/skills.ts`: `ailment_burst`, `leaveClouds`; `src/sim/run.ts`: `stepClouds`; ordinary Blight applies once, Wandering Rot persists and reapplies, Spore Burst hits, overlapping areas may affect the same enemy.

text.name: Cone
text.means: A wedge aimed toward your target. A standard Cone hit deals full damage to every enemy inside it, with no target limit. Reach determines its distance and angle determines its width. At 360°, it covers every direction. Alternate modes can replace the wedge or its initial hit.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/skills.ts`: `cone`, `inWedge`; uncapped targets, full standard hit, angle capped at 360 degrees; Fissure and Tremor replace geometry/delivery.

text.name: Convert
text.means: A tree conversion changes the skill's base damage to the stated type. Damage-type and Ailment modifiers in that skill's tree change to match. Gear modifiers keep their original types, and added damage of other types remains unless a separate conversion applies. A conversion of a stated share moves only that share of the specified damage; the converted part scales with its new type.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/stats.ts`: `damageBreakdown`, `convertedType`, `retag`, `treeMod`, `effectiveSkill`; base/tree conversion differs from partial added-damage conversion. Gear keeps tags; unrelated added damage survives.

text.name: Critical
text.means: A Critical hit normally deals 200% of its usual damage. Critical Damage adds to that total: +50% Critical Damage makes it 250%. Critical Chance determines how often a skill is Critical. Increased Critical Chance scales the base chance; 10% base chance with 50% increased becomes 15%. Ailment ticks do not deal Critical damage.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/stats.ts`: `playerStats`; `src/sim/run.ts`: `dealDamage`, `critChanceOf`, `stepAilments`; normal hit multiplier 2 + Critical Damage / 100, increased base Critical Chance, no Critical damage on ticks, crit-into-buff is an exception.

text.name: Curse
text.means: Dark hits use your chance to apply Curse. By default, each stack lasts 8s. When a Cursed enemy dies, it deals Dark damage equal to 4% of its maximum Life per stack to other enemies within 2.2 tiles.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/data.ts`: Curse definition; `src/sim/run.ts`: `strike`, `burstCurse`; base 8s, enemy death releases Dark damage of 4% maximum Life per stack, 2.2-tile radius, each recipient's Resistance; Starved can scale it.

text.name: Dodge
text.means: Dodging avoids all damage from an ordinary enemy hit. Dodge Chance is capped at 50%. Ailment damage, boss room attacks and boss drains bypass Dodge. Converting Armour to Dodge removes the damage reduction that Armour would have provided.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/stats.ts`: `playerStats`; `src/sim/run.ts`: `dealDamage`, `bite`, `stepAilments`; 50% cap, ordinary hit avoidance, Armour conversion removes reduction; boss room damage and ticks do not roll Dodge.

text.name: Echo
text.means: Each Echo hits a different enemy near your original melee target, choosing the nearest first. By default, it deals 70% of the full hit damage. The first Echo can reach 1.5 tiles from the original target; each additional Echo extends this limit by 0.6 tiles. Echoes do not target the original enemy.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/skills.ts`: `melee`; nearest other enemies, 70% default share, 1.5 + 0.6 times prior Echo count in tiles, measured from original target. Removed whole-use uniqueness claim because Repeats/carry/Splash can hit again.

text.name: Exposure
text.means: Light hits use your chance to apply Exposure. By default, each stack lasts 5s and causes 4% increased damage taken from hits. Stack bonuses add together. Exposure does not increase damage taken from Ailment ticks.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/data.ts`: Exposure definition; `src/sim/run.ts`: `dealDamage`, `stepAilments`; base 5s, additive 4% increased hit damage taken per stack, no increased Ailment tick damage; magnitude/protection modifiers may apply.

text.name: Fork
text.means: Each Fork creates a separate bolt that strikes an enemy near your original target, within 3.2 tiles. It deals 45% of the full hit damage unless modified. Forks choose the nearest enemies that the use has not already hit directly. They can strike in any direction from the original target.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/skills.ts`: `projectile`; nearest unhit targets within 3.2 tiles of original target, one per Fork, default 45% share, independent of shot direction.

text.name: Gust
text.means: Gale starts with 3 Gusts. Each grants 10% more Movement Speed by default; these bonuses add together. Taking a hit removes one Gust and restarts the recovery timer. Boss drains remove Gusts too. One Gust returns every 6s, up to your maximum. Gale talents can change these values or prevent Gust loss.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. W020: `src/sim/movers.ts`: `moverStats`; `RunSim.stepGusts`, `spendGust`, `paceOf`, `bite`; base three, additive 10% per Gust within separate movement multiplier, six-second recovery restarted on loss; boss drains also consume Gusts despite hit-only source wording. | Returned to pending: decision recorded in BLOCKERS.md.

text.name: increased / reduced
text.means: For stats with a base value, increased and reduced modifiers add together before multiplying that base, including flat additions. Two 50% increased modifiers give 100% increased, doubling the value. Reduced modifiers subtract from that total. Added chance bonuses, such as +10% chance to apply an Ailment, add percentage points instead.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/mods.ts`: `aggregate`, `computeStat`, `percentStat`; additive increases/reductions multiply base plus flats; added chance bonuses use percentage points.

text.name: more / less
text.means: Separate more and less modifiers multiply. Two 50% more modifiers give 2.25 times the original value, or 125% more. A 40% less modifier multiplies the value by 0.6. Bonuses that a description says add together, such as bonuses per stack, are combined before their multiplier applies.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/mods.ts`: `computeStat`; `src/sim/grants.ts`: family merge rules; `src/sim/run.ts`: `hasteOf`, `paceOf`; separate factors multiply, explicitly summed per-stack/family bonuses combine first.

text.name: Pierce
text.means: Allows a Projectile to hit additional enemies behind its target. Each Pierce adds one target within 4.5 tiles beyond the original target and 0.85 tiles either side of the shot's path. Each Pierced enemy takes 70% of the full hit damage unless a skill or modifier changes that share.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/data.ts`: `PROJECTILE`; `src/sim/skills.ts`: `alongRay`, `projectile`, `hailOf`; target count, original-target corridor, 4.5-tile extension and default 70% share confirmed.

text.name: Poison
text.means: Poison deals damage over time. You apply it through skills and effects that specifically inflict it. Its source determines its damage and duration. Poison ticks do not deal Critical damage. With Contagion, each tick uses your Critical Chance to try to spread Poison.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/skills.ts`: `ailment_burst`; `src/sim/run.ts`: `applyAilment`, `stepAilments`, `spreadAilment`; source defines damage/duration, including typed added damage; tick Critical Chance only triggers Contagion and never Critical Damage.

text.name: Projectile
text.means: The standard Projectile use hits your target. Each additional Projectile hits a different enemy within 3.5 tiles of that target for full damage, before Spread modifiers. These direct hits do not hit the same enemy twice in one use. Splash and Bursts can overlap. Alternate skill modes can change this targeting and damage.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/skills.ts`: `projectile`, `spreadTargets`, `fanOut`, `fallOn`, `strikeShocked`; ordinary direct hits share a visited set, extra shots have full share, Splash/Bursts can overlap, alternate modes replace delivery.

text.name: Repeat
text.means: Each Repeat adds another attack within the same use, without another Mana cost. A standard melee Repeat hits your original target for full damage and stops if that target dies. Alternate modes can repeat the whole attack pattern, such as a spin or thrown blade.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/skills.ts`: `melee`, `throwBlades`, `spin`; `src/sim/run.ts`: `swing`; one Mana payment per use, ordinary repeated hits stop on primary death, alternate attacks repeat their pattern.

text.name: Resistance
text.means: Resistance reduces damage from the corresponding damage type, including damage over time. Each Resistance is capped at 75%. Resistance and Armour apply separately to hits: 50% damage reduction from each leaves you taking 25% of the incoming damage.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/stats.ts`: `resistancesFrom`; `src/sim/run.ts`: `afterResistance`, `dealDamage`, `bite`, `stepAilments`; per-type 75% cap, applies to damage over time, multiplies separately from Armour.

text.name: Shock
text.means: Lightning hits use your chance to apply Shock. Each stack you apply deals 7 base Lightning damage per second for 4s, before Ailment damage and duration modifiers. Spell Damage, Attack Damage and Critical Damage do not increase this damage.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. W021: `RunSim.shockArc` selects monsters when carrier is hero, but only the hero when carrier is monster. This contradicts the nearby-enemy rule. Confirmed base 7 Lightning DPS for 4s is rewritten; secondary targeting awaits Claude. | Returned to pending: decision recorded in BLOCKERS.md.

text.name: Slow
text.means: Temporarily reduces Attack and Cast Speed by the amount stated on the effect. A 30% Slow makes attacks and casts occur at 70% of their normal rate. Slow deals no damage.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/run.ts`: `slowFor`, `hasteOf`, `stepEffects`, Heavy Hand and Block Stagger consumers; reduces Attack/Cast rate by stated share for effect duration; does not reduce damage. Movement is not claimed (W018).

text.name: Splash
text.means: A skill with Splash deals a share of its hit damage to other enemies in a circle around the enemy hit. The skill lists its base damage share and radius. Splash does not hit the central target again, but Splashes from separate hits can overlap.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/skills.ts`: `splashFrom`; requires a skill's `splash` definition, excludes the central target, uses listed share and area-scaled radius; repeated hits can overlap their Splashes.

text.name: Spread
text.means: The distance from your original target within which additional Projectiles can choose enemies. The base distance is 3.5 tiles. Spread modifiers scale this distance directly; Area of Effect does not affect it.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/sim/skills.ts`: `spreadTargets`; `PROJECTILE.spread * spreadRange`, measured from original target; no `areaRadius` call.

text.name: Starved
text.means: When you cannot pay the full Mana cost, you spend your remaining Mana and use the skill anyway. Starved hits deal 50% of their normal damage before modifiers to the penalty. An effect that pays the missing cost with Life prevents Starved. Blight's Poison bypasses this penalty.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. W005: `RunSim.swing`, `weak`, `dealDamage`, `applyAilment`; confirmed insufficient-Mana trigger, remaining-Mana payment, 50% default hit share and Life-payment exception; Blight Poison bypasses the penalty, contrary to broad talent promises. | Returned to pending: decision recorded in BLOCKERS.md.

text.name: Stun
text.means: Prevents an enemy from moving, attacking or casting for the stated duration. If you have an effect that grants Stun, hits dealing a larger share of maximum Life have a higher Stun chance. Before Stun chance modifiers, a hit dealing 10% of maximum Life has about 3% chance to Stun; a hit dealing 80% has about 72%. Killing hits always trigger your Stun effects when you can Stun.

notes: Full glossary batch; writing/GLOSSARY.md. `src/data.ts`: `stunChanceFor`; `src/sim/run.ts`: `stun`, `stepMonster`, `dealDamage`; requires Stun grant, chance is damage/maxLife to power 1.5 before modifiers, killing-hit trigger, movement/action lock for duration.

text.said: I keep a shelf here. Shards, mostly. Come and look when you have the gold.
You went all the way down. Nobody has done that and come back up past me. I had stopped watching the stair.
So there is nothing under it after all. Only more of it, and it wants something else from you now.
Here. I have been keeping these two for whoever finished it, and I had begun to think that was nobody.
Now this. I have been keeping it for whoever came back up enough times, and that is you.
Carry one of these down and the Fissure goes on. And on. Same crack, same rock, and it does not end when it used to end. I have never worked out where the extra comes from.
And it changes, the longer you hold it. Slowly. Whatever you feed it, it wants the same thing again.
Another one. They come up out of the wall down there faster than I can carry them.
Take it. I have stopped asking what it is I am handing you.
Going down. Everyone is, when they come past me. Most of them are only going down the once.
It does not end where you think it ends. There is always another way further in, and the things in it take their opinions from somewhere deeper than you.
Do not go with nothing in your hands. Take this one — I have carried it a long way and it has never once been any use to me.
The stair behind me keeps going. I stopped following it. You will not.
You came back up. Most do not, and none of them wanted this.
Everything I have worked out about what is down there is in it — what a thing is called, and what it does. Keep it. Add to it.

text.seen: A lantern, further back than you have been. Something is holding it up.

text.said: The Rot gave up something when you finished it. It was in the wall this morning and it was not there last night.
Put it in the rock beside the crystals. Everything down there starts again, and none of it will be as easy as it was.

text.name: The Answering
text.said: You say the three marks out loud. Something a long way off in the dark stops, and turns round.
It was already standing there. It has been standing there the whole time.
Oh. Oh, no.

text.name: The Flowering
text.said: The floor is soft. Everything growing on it is leaning the same way, towards the middle.
All of this came after the rock. All of it came out of one thing.
And it has been waiting for somebody to walk this far in.

text.name: the Astral-Geometer
text.said: Something turning, slowly, and a long way in. Somebody hung it there.
text.greets: Stand still. No — exactly there, you are holding the angle. Right. It reads the same here as it does in nine other rooms. I stay where the reading is. Bring me dust and come back down.
text.idles: No dust? Then there is nothing to measure, and we are both wasting the light.

text.said: Do not put that down. Hold it where the light is — there, you see the angle it makes. It makes that angle everywhere. Nine rooms, and never once wrong.
The other one takes bodies. I take the dust, which is what is left when the rock has finished deciding. A body is an opinion. Dust is a measurement.
I will set it into something small of yours. Small, because the angle does not care how much of it there is. Give me a ring, or the thing at your throat, and I will show you.

text.name: the Osteomancer
text.said: Somebody has been sorting down here. The sorting is not finished.
text.greets: Feet. FEET. Half of that was in order and I have been at it since the lamp was lit. You are too big, I do not try. I do not go up. You come back down to me and bring one that came apart right.
text.idles: Nothing on you. Nothing at all on you. Go down. Bring me one that came apart RIGHT. Then we talk.

text.said: You have one. You have one on you, I hear it not rotting. Give here. Give here — no. Hold it up. Let me look first.
They come apart WRONG down here. All of them. Not this one. This one came apart right, and a thing that came apart right was still deciding when it stopped, and a thing still deciding can be ASKED.
I put it in something of yours. Not on top. IN. Whatever the smith meant that piece to be, it stops being that, and it is this now. You pick which one. I do not care which one.

text.name: The Glasswright
text.said: A room somebody swept. The walls are covered in marks and none of them are yours.
text.greets: Do not touch the wall. You are standing in the middle of a sentence and you cannot read it. Come and find me above and I will tell you whose it is.
text.idles: Set more of them in the wall. Read a little further, and then I will hand you the rest of it.

text.said: Stop. Before you set another one of those in the wall — do you know what he has you doing?
They are not fuel. They are punctuation. He has you reading a sentence out loud, one mark at a time, and he has never once asked what it says.

Everything down here has a true name and can be told. That is the Obsidian Order, and I am the last of us this far down. This one I have written out for you — three marks, copied off a wall nobody was meant to reach.
Set it in the wall the way you set the others and say it where the rock is thin. It will turn round. Then you will know which of us has been right, and it will not be him.

text.name: The Refraction
text.said: Every surface in here is holding the same light, and all of it is pointing at one place.
The walls have been getting brighter for an hour. This is where it was going.
It is not reflecting anything. It is the thing being reflected.

text.name: the Smith
text.said: Somebody has been working down here, and recently. The stone is still warm.
text.greets: You walked past three seams to get here. Three. Come up and see me when you are done and I will put something in your hand that can take them.
text.idles: Wear it out. Then we will talk about what comes after it.

text.said: You came down that ladder with nothing on your belt. Nothing. No wonder the walls are still full.
There is ore in here, and hide on the things that come at you, and fibre where the damp is. All of it stays where it is unless you are carrying the thing that takes it.
Pick one and it is yours. The others I will sell you, and when you have worn one down far enough to have learned something, bring it back and I will make it better.

text.name: the Lampwright
text.said: A lantern, further back than you have been. Something is holding it up.
text.greets: Do not put it out. Do NOT — thank you. That is eleven hours of lamp and I am not walking back up in the dark. I keep a bench at the top; come and find me.

text.name: Aftershock
text.description: Every Ailment on an enemy also deals 50% of each tick to enemies within 2.2 tiles of it, and your Ailments last 40% less time.

text.said: I began with one shard, and the angle it made where it broke. Then the next one. Then the next.
Nine rooms. A hundred and forty shards, measured against each other. Not once a different angle.
So I hung the thing that would be wrong if I were. It has been turning ever since and it has not been wrong.
The other one takes bodies. I take the dust, which is what is left when the rock has finished deciding.
A body is an opinion. Dust is a measurement, and a measurement will fit inside a ring.
He touches your arm and his head comes into yours. It is soft at first. A boy came down here for the work. Nineteen. Boy had a lamp. Boy had food for a season.
Food gone. Lamp gone. Then boy finds the other thing there is down here. Boy does not say it out loud. Boy just does it.
Hands went first. Hands went first and hands never asked him. Head stayed boy a long while after. Head sat and watched hands.
Then head goes too. No hurt in it. No fight in it. Something down in boy said YES, and boy stopped being boy.
Now it is all mine. All of it, in rows, and I know every one by the sound it makes. I am good. I am the BEST there is at this.
You are too big. Too big, too bright, I do not try, no. But you go down and things stop down there — bring the stopped ones to ME. I give good things back. I have SO many good things.
There were nine of us who could read it. We came down together to copy the wall out, and we agreed on almost nothing else.
The others went back up. I stayed. Two hundred and eleven marks on the one wall, and all of it is a single sentence.
Reading it was not enough. So I set the first of them into myself, to find out whether it would read back.
It read back. After that I stopped deciding how many there should be, and the rock decided instead.
Three marks, copied off a face nobody was meant to reach. I have been waiting a long while for somebody to carry them.
I came down for the ore. There is more of it in this rock than anybody above has ever wanted to believe.
I made them for the men who would come down here and buy them. Not one of those men ever came down.
What came down instead was the rest of the working, and it had been here a good deal longer than the ore had.
So I found out what my own work is worth. It is worth a great deal.
And I have been down here ever since, making the next one.
Four days on that ledge with the lamp out and nothing coming. Then you. I am not going to forget which of us walked down there.
Nothing down there troubles a body that keeps moving, so I moved for a long while. I would rather stand still now, at your fire, and owe you for it.
I can smelt, weave, tan, cook and cut, and down there not one of the five was worth anything. Up here they are yours.
I came down for the glass and the glass kept me, and I had stopped counting. You got me out. Put me to work and we are square.
I went in a long time ago, to see how far it went. I had a lamp and I had a season of food.
The season went. The rock changed twice and kept going. And then, at last, I thought I had found the end of it.
What I had found was that something down there was alive, and that it had been waiting a great deal longer than I had been walking.

text.name: Hob
text.greets: Get me up out of this and I will work whatever you put in front of me.

text.name: Ida
text.greets: Nothing here eats a body that keeps moving. I have been moving. Let me stop, at your camp.

text.name: Nell
text.greets: Three days down here. I can smelt, weave, tan, cook or cut. Take me up.

text.name: Wat
text.greets: I came down for the glass and the glass kept me. Show me the way out and I am yours.
